raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

This PR adds a `sparse_disk` weight transfer backend. The trainer writes each round's sparse patches to a safetensors file on storage shared with the inference workers, and the workers apply the patches in place.

It covers the sparse, update-from-disk part of #48644. I described the idea there first: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48644#issuecomment-6008358757.

## Claims

- You can send sparse patches without an NCCL group between the trainer and the inference servers, and without a GPU on the trainer.
- The trainer API is the same as `sparse_nccl`: the same `SparseWeightPatch`, `send_weights(patches)` and `send_weight_chunk(patches)`. Only the transport changes.
- Workers reject any safetensors file that is not a patch file. Pointing the backend at a full checkpoint by mistake fails without touching the model.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py -v \
  -k "sparse_disk or sparse_nccl or Factory"
```

On main `2bea2200` plus this change (Linux, CPU, torch 2.13.0): **19 passed, 1 skipped**. The skip is the existing GPU-only `sparse_nccl` test. Three of the tests are new, and all three run on CPU:

- A trainer engine and a worker engine, both built through the factories and joined by an in-process client, move a two-tensor patch end to end. Only the addressed elements change, and no patch file is left behind.
- The worker rejects a safetensors file that does not carry the patch format marker.
- A trainer rank that is not the sender writes no file and makes no RPC.

`mypy` on the new module and `ruff check` / `ruff format` on the changed Python files are clean.

**End to end on a GPU** (1x L4, main `2bea2200` plus this change, torch 2.13.0+cu130). I ran `vllm serve <model> --weight-transfer-config '{"backend": "sparse_disk"}'` and built the trainer engine with `WeightTransferTrainerFactory.trainer_init` and an `HTTPVLLMWeightSyncClient`. The patches are bit-exact diffs between BF16 checkpoints from three real AdamW steps (lr 1e-6). To compare weights, I hashed every parameter and buffer on the worker.

| | Qwen3-0.6B | SmolLM2-360M | TinyLlama-1.1B |
|---|---|---|---|
| checkpoint | 1.5 GB | 724 MB | 2.2 GB |
| elements changed per step | 1.1-1.5% | 0.24-0.36% | 1.9-2.6% |
| patch payload per step | 51-69 MB | 5-8 MB | 128-174 MB |
| `send_weights` (write file + update) | 0.23-0.38 s | 0.16-0.32 s | 0.26-0.45 s |
| `reload_weights`, same server | 0.77-1.18 s | 0.46-0.78 s | 0.89-1.22 s |
| 3 patches vs `reload_weights`, same server | 0 of 340 differ | 0 of 324 differ | 0 of 224 differ |
| 3 patches vs cold start on the target | 0 of 340 differ | 0 of 324 differ | 0 of 224 differ |
| v0 -> v3 as two `send_weight_chunk` calls vs the 3 patches | 0 differ | 0 differ | 0 differ |
| greedy outputs, patched vs `reload_weights`, same server | 8 of 8 identical | 8 of 8 identical | 8 of 8 identical |

No patch file was left in `patch_dir` after any run. The timings are single measurements on a local disk, so read them as rough. I only compared outputs within one server process.

Qwen3-0.6B ties `lm_head` to the embedding, and its checkpoint lists both names, so I left `lm_head.weight` out of the patches. If I keep it in, the update fails with the #60151 error (`'lm_head.weight' was skipped because it is tied to 'model.embed_tokens.weight' ...`). #60188 fixes that.

## Details

**Why a separate backend.** `sparse_nccl` needs a GPU and an NCCL rendezvous on the trainer. When the trainer and the inference servers run separately, a filesystem is often the only thing they share. Sparse patches are small (1 to 3 percent of elements per AdamW step in my runs), so a file is a cheap way to move them.

**How it works.**

- Each update is one file. It holds tensors `{i}.indices` and `{i}.values`, and the names and full shapes go in the safetensors metadata under `format = vllm-sparse-patch-v1`. The file is written under a `.partial` name and then renamed, so a worker never reads a half-written file.
- The worker engine keeps no state. `init`, `start` and `finish` do nothing, as in `sparse_nccl`. `receive_weights` loads the file onto the worker's device and calls `load_checkpoint_weight_patches`, so TP slicing and packed parameters go through the model's own loader.
- The trainer engine writes the file under `patch_dir`, calls `update_weights` with its absolute path, and deletes the file when the call returns.
- `save_sparse_patches` and `load_sparse_patches` are public, so an orchestrator that wants to manage the files itself can do that.

**Why this is not a duplicate.**

- #52152 (draft) adds a `disk` backend that reloads a whole checkpoint directory through the layerwise path. This PR sends sparse patches that are applied in place. The two share no code.
- `modelexpress` installs published weight versions through an external service. This backend needs nothing beyond safetensors.
- I checked `gh pr list --state open --search "48644 in:body"` and `--search "sparse disk weight transfer"` on 2026-10-10.

**Limits.**

- The sparse loader's limits apply: floating-point, unquantized weights, where the final copy has the same shape as the checkpoint tensor.
- Models with tied embeddings need #60188 (the fix for #60151) when a patch carries both names.
- Each TP rank reads the whole file. There is no rollback after a partial failure, same as `sparse_nccl`.
- Workers open whatever path `update_weights` names. The docs say to expose the weight transfer endpoints only to trusted callers. I did not add a configured root directory because I wanted to leave `WeightTransferConfig` alone, but I'm happy to add one if you prefer.
- An update needs free GPU memory on every rank: the patch, plus the loader's full checkpoint-shaped tensor for the largest weight. Llama-3.1-8B ran out of memory at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85` and passed at 0.6.
- Tested with tensor parallelism up to 4 (see the comment below). Not tested: pipeline or expert parallelism, a network filesystem, several replicas reading the same patch file.

Size: 167 lines of code in the new module (242 with docstrings), plus 19 lines in the factory and config.

+# Sparse Disk Engine
+
+The `sparse_disk` weight transfer engine applies sparse, flat-index weight
+patches that the trainer writes to a file on storage shared with the inference
+workers. It carries the same patches as [sparse NCCL](nccl.md#sparse-nccl) and
+applies them the same way; only the transport differs.
+
+## When to Use Sparse Disk
+
+- Training and inference are disaggregated and share a filesystem (a network
+  volume, or a local disk when they are colocated) but not an NCCL group.
+- The trainer has no GPU, or should not hold a GPU communicator open.
+- Each update changes a small fraction of the weights, so a patch is much
+  smaller than a checkpoint.
+
+## How It Works
+
+1. The trainer writes the round's patches to one safetensors file under
+   `patch_dir`. The file appears under its final name only once it is complete.
+2. The trainer calls `update_weights` with the file's absolute path.
+3. Every inference worker reads the file onto its device and applies it through
+   the model's native `load_weights()`, which maps checkpoint coordinates to
+   rank-local tensor-parallel and packed runtime parameters.
+4. The trainer deletes the file once the call returns.
+
+Patches are applied in place, so the layerwise reload lifecycle is not used and
+`start_weight_update` and `finish_weight_update` are no-ops.
+
+## Usage
+
+Select the backend on the inference side:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve my-model \
+    --weight-transfer-config '{"backend": "sparse_disk"}'
+```
+
+On the trainer side, build the engine once and send each round's patches:
+
+```python
+from vllm.distributed.weight_transfer import (
+    HTTPVLLMWeightSyncClient,
+    WeightTransferTrainerFactory,
+)
+from vllm.distributed.weight_transfer.sparse_disk_engine import (
+    SparseDiskTrainerInitInfo,
+)
+from vllm.distributed.weight_transfer.sparse_nccl_engine import SparseWeightPatch
+
+engine = WeightTransferTrainerFactory.trainer_init(
+    init_info=SparseDiskTrainerInitInfo(patch_dir="/shared/patches", rank=0),
+    client=HTTPVLLMWeightSyncClient("http://localhost:8000"),
+)
+
+engine.send_weights(
+    [
+        SparseWeightPatch(
+            name="model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight",
+            indices=flat_indices,           # int32 or int64, 1-D
+            values=new_values,              # same length as indices
+            full_shape=tuple(param.shape),
+        )
+    ]
+)
+```
+
+Each `send_weights(patches)` call owns a complete `start` / `update` / `finish`
+lifecycle. As with sparse NCCL, `send_weight_chunk(patches)` sends one chunk
+inside a lifecycle the caller owns.
+
+`patch_dir` must already exist and be visible at the same absolute path to the
+trainer and to every inference worker.
+
+## Patch File Format
+
+A patch file is a safetensors file whose metadata has `format` set to
+`vllm-sparse-patch-v1` and `patches` set to a JSON list of
+`{"name": ..., "shape": [...]}` entries. Entry `i` has two tensors, `{i}.indices`
+and `{i}.values`. Names, shapes, and indices are in checkpoint coordinates.
+
+A process that does not use the trainer engine can write files with
+`save_sparse_patches` and pass their paths to `update_weights` itself.
+
+## Limitations
+
+- The limits of the sparse loader apply: floating-point, unquantized weights
+  whose final load step is a same-shaped copy.
+- Every worker reads the whole file, so with tensor parallelism it is read once
+  per rank.
+- An update needs free GPU memory on every rank: the patch, plus the loader's
+  full checkpoint-shaped tensor for the largest weight. Leave headroom with
+  `--gpu-memory-utilization`.
+- The caller owns diffing and restart or reseed after a partial failure. A
+  failed update does not roll back patches that were already applied.
+- Workers open whatever path `update_weights` names. Expose the weight transfer
+  endpoints only to trusted callers.

     assert client.order == []
 
 
+# --- Sparse Disk ---
+
+
+class _CheckpointModel(torch.nn.Module):
+    """A model whose `load_weights` copies checkpoint tensors onto same-named
+    parameters, standing in for a real model's native loader."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.w = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(2, 3), requires_grad=False)
+        self.b = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(4), requires_grad=False)
+
+    def load_weights(self, weights):
+        loaded = set()
+        for name, tensor in weights:
+            self.get_parameter(name).data.copy_(tensor)
+            loaded.add(name)
+        return loaded
+
+
+class _WorkerClient:
+    """A VLLMWeightSyncClient that drives one in-process worker engine."""
+
+    def __init__(self, model: torch.nn.Module):
+        self.engine = WeightTransferEngineFactory.create_engine(
+            WeightTransferConfig(backend="sparse_disk"),
+            create_mock_vllm_config(),
+            torch.device("cpu"),
+            model,
+        )
+
+    def init_weight_transfer_engine(self, init_info: dict) -> None:
+        self.engine.init_transfer_engine(self.engine.parse_init_info(init_info))
+
+    def start_weight_update(self) -> None:
+        self.engine.start_weight_update()
+
+    def update_weights(self, update_info: dict) -> None:
+        self.engine.receive_weights(self.engine.parse_update_info(update_info))
+
+    def finish_weight_update(self, weight_version: str | None = None) -> None:
+        self.engine.finish_weight_update()
+
+
+def test_sparse_disk_patches_reach_worker_model(tmp_path):
+    """Patches sent by the trainer engine change only the addressed elements of
+    the worker's model, and no patch file outlives the round."""
+    model = _CheckpointModel()
+    trainer = WeightTransferTrainerFactory.trainer_init(
+        init_info=SparseDiskTrainerInitInfo(patch_dir=str(tmp_path), rank=0),
+        client=_WorkerClient(model),
+    )
+
+    trainer.send_weights(
+        [
+            SparseWeightPatch(
+                name="w",
+                indices=torch.tensor([1, 5], dtype=torch.int32),
+                values=torch.tensor([1.5, -2.0]),
+                full_shape=(2, 3),
+            ),
+            SparseWeightPatch(
+                name="b",
+                indices=torch.tensor([3], dtype=torch.int32),
+                values=torch.tensor([7.0]),
+                full_shape=(4,),
+            ),
+        ]
+    )
+
+    assert torch.equal(model.w, torch.tensor([[0.0, 1.5, 0.0], [0.0, 0.0, -2.0]]))
+    assert torch.equal(model.b, torch.tensor([0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 7.0]))
+    assert list(tmp_path.iterdir()) == []
+
+
+def test_sparse_disk_worker_rejects_other_safetensors_files(tmp_path):
+    """Pointing the worker at a full checkpoint must fail without loading it."""
+    from safetensors.torch import save_file
+
+    checkpoint = tmp_path / "model.safetensors"
+    save_file({"w": torch.ones(2, 3)}, checkpoint)
+    model = _CheckpointModel()
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="sparse patch file"):
+        _WorkerClient(model).update_weights({"patch_path": str(checkpoint)})
+    assert torch.equal(model.w, torch.zeros(2, 3))
+
+
+def test_sparse_disk_trainer_non_sender_writes_nothing(tmp_path):
+    client = RecordingClient()
+    engine = WeightTransferTrainerFactory.trainer_init(
+        init_info=SparseDiskTrainerInitInfo(patch_dir=str(tmp_path), rank=1),
+        client=client,
+    )
+
+    engine.send_weights([_sparse_patch()])
+    engine.send_weight_chunk([_sparse_patch()])
+
+    assert client.order == []
+    assert list(tmp_path.iterdir()) == []
+

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Sparse disk weight transfer engine.
+
+The trainer writes each round's sparse patches to one safetensors file on
+storage that every inference worker can read at the same path. Workers apply the
+file through the model's native weight loader, as the sparse NCCL backend does.
+"""
+
+import json
+import os
+import uuid
+from collections.abc import Iterable
+from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import ClassVar, Self
+
+import torch
+from safetensors import safe_open
+from safetensors.torch import save_file
+
+from vllm.distributed.weight_transfer.base import (
+    TrainerInitInfo,
+    TrainerWeightTransferEngine,
+    VLLMWeightSyncClient,
+    WeightSource,
+    WeightTransferEngine,
+    WeightTransferInitInfo,
+    WeightTransferUpdateInfo,
+)
+from vllm.distributed.weight_transfer.sparse_nccl_engine import SparseWeightPatch
+from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.checkpoint_weight_patch import (
+    CheckpointWeightPatch,
+    load_checkpoint_weight_patches,
+)
+
+__all__ = [
+    "SparseDiskTrainerInitInfo",
+    "SparseDiskTrainerWeightTransferEngine",
+    "SparseDiskWeightTransferEngine",
+    "SparseDiskWeightTransferInitInfo",
+    "SparseDiskWeightTransferUpdateInfo",
+    "load_sparse_patches",
+    "save_sparse_patches",
+]
+
+PATCH_FORMAT = "vllm-sparse-patch-v1"
+
+
+def save_sparse_patches(patches: Iterable[SparseWeightPatch], path: str | Path) -> None:
+    """Write sparse patches to one safetensors file.
+
+    Patch `i` is stored as tensors `{i}.indices` and `{i}.values`; names and full
+    checkpoint shapes are in the file metadata. The file appears at `path` only
+    once it is complete.
+    """
+    path = Path(path)
+    tensors: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}
+    entries = []
+    for i, patch in enumerate(patches):
+        tensors[f"{i}.indices"] = patch.indices.detach().cpu()
+        tensors[f"{i}.values"] = patch.values.detach().cpu()
+        entries.append({"name": patch.name, "shape": list(patch.full_shape)})
+    partial = path.with_name(f"{path.name}.partial")
+    save_file(
+        tensors,
+        partial,
+        metadata={"format": PATCH_FORMAT, "patches": json.dumps(entries)},
+    )
+    os.replace(partial, path)
+
+
+def load_sparse_patches(
+    path: str | Path, device: torch.device | str = "cpu"
+) -> list[CheckpointWeightPatch]:
+    """Read a file written by `save_sparse_patches` onto `device`."""
+    with safe_open(path, framework="pt", device=str(device)) as file:
+        metadata = file.metadata() or {}
+        if metadata.get("format") != PATCH_FORMAT:
+            raise ValueError(f"Not a {PATCH_FORMAT} sparse patch file: {path}")
+        patches = []
+        for i, entry in enumerate(json.loads(metadata["patches"])):
+            values = file.get_tensor(f"{i}.values")
+            patches.append(
+                CheckpointWeightPatch(
+                    name=entry["name"],
+                    shape=tuple(entry["shape"]),
+                    dtype=values.dtype,
+                    values=values,
+                    indices=file.get_tensor(f"{i}.indices"),
+                )
+            )
+    return patches
+
+
+@dataclass
+class SparseDiskWeightTransferInitInfo(WeightTransferInitInfo):
+    """Init info for the sparse disk backend. There is nothing to rendezvous."""
+
+
+@dataclass
+class SparseDiskWeightTransferUpdateInfo(WeightTransferUpdateInfo):
+    """Update info for the sparse disk backend."""
+
+    patch_path: str
+    """Absolute path of a patch file, readable by every inference worker."""
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        if not os.path.isabs(self.patch_path):
+            raise ValueError(f"`patch_path` must be absolute: {self.patch_path}")
+
+
+class SparseDiskWeightTransferEngine(
+    WeightTransferEngine[
+        SparseDiskWeightTransferInitInfo, SparseDiskWeightTransferUpdateInfo
+    ]
+):
+    """Sparse weight transfer engine reading patch files from shared storage.
+
+    Applies checkpoint-coordinate patches through the model's native weight
+    loader. Sparse updates modify initialized model tensors in place, so the
+    layerwise reload lifecycle is not used.
+    """
+
+    init_info_cls = SparseDiskWeightTransferInitInfo
+    update_info_cls = SparseDiskWeightTransferUpdateInfo
+    supports_draft_weight_update = False
+
+    def init_transfer_engine(self, init_info: SparseDiskWeightTransferInitInfo) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    def start_weight_update(self) -> None:
+        """No-op: sparse patches are applied in place, no layerwise reload."""
+        pass
+
+    def finish_weight_update(self) -> None:
+        """No-op: sparse patches are applied in place, no layerwise reload."""
+        pass
+
+    def receive_weights(self, update_info: SparseDiskWeightTransferUpdateInfo) -> None:
+        patches = load_sparse_patches(update_info.patch_path, self.device)
+        load_checkpoint_weight_patches(self.model, patches)
+
+    def shutdown(self) -> None:
+        pass
+
+
+@dataclass
+class SparseDiskTrainerInitInfo(TrainerInitInfo):
+    """Trainer-side init info for the sparse disk weight transfer backend."""
+
+    backend: ClassVar[str] = "sparse_disk"
+
+    patch_dir: str
+    """Existing directory the trainer writes patch files to. Every inference
+    worker must see it at the same absolute path."""
+
+
+class SparseDiskTrainerWeightTransferEngine(
+    TrainerWeightTransferEngine[SparseDiskTrainerInitInfo]
+):
+    """Trainer-side sparse disk weight transfer engine.
+
+    Writes each call's patches to a new file under `patch_dir`, has the inference
+    workers apply it, then deletes the file. The send methods and their patch
+    type match `SparseNCCLTrainerWeightTransferEngine`; only the transport
+    differs, so no GPU or NCCL group is needed on the trainer.
+    """
+
+    init_info_cls = SparseDiskTrainerInitInfo
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        client: VLLMWeightSyncClient,
+        patch_dir: str | Path,
+        source: WeightSource | None = None,
+        is_sender: bool = True,
+    ) -> None:
+        if source is not None:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Sparse disk weight transfer takes no WeightSource; pass each "
+                "round's patches to send_weights(patches) instead."
+            )
+        super().__init__(client=client, source=source, is_sender=is_sender)
+        self.patch_dir = Path(patch_dir).absolute()
+
+    @classmethod
+    def trainer_init(
+        cls,
+        init_info: SparseDiskTrainerInitInfo,
+        *,
+        client: VLLMWeightSyncClient,
+        source: WeightSource | None = None,
+    ) -> Self:
+        engine = cls(
+            client=client,
+            patch_dir=init_info.patch_dir,
+            source=source,
+            is_sender=init_info.is_sender,
+        )
+        if engine.is_sender:
+            client.init_weight_transfer_engine(
+                asdict(SparseDiskWeightTransferInitInfo())
+            )
+        return engine
+
+    def send_weights(self, patches: Iterable[SparseWeightPatch] | None = None) -> None:
+        """Send one sparse update through a one-shot lifecycle."""
+        patches = self._prepare_patches(patches)
+        if not patches:
+            return
+
+        self.client.start_weight_update()
+        self._send_chunk(patches)
+        self.client.finish_weight_update()
+
+    def send_weight_chunk(
+        self, patches: Iterable[SparseWeightPatch] | None = None
+    ) -> None:
+        """Send one chunk inside a caller-owned weight update lifecycle."""
+        patches = self._prepare_patches(patches)
+        if not patches:
+            return
+        self._send_chunk(patches)
+
+    def _prepare_patches(
+        self, patches: Iterable[SparseWeightPatch] | None
+    ) -> list[SparseWeightPatch]:
+        if not self.is_sender or patches is None:
+            return []
+        return list(patches)
+
+    def _send_chunk(self, patches: list[SparseWeightPatch]) -> None:
+        path = self.patch_dir / f"patch-{uuid.uuid4().hex}.safetensors"
+        save_sparse_patches(patches, path)
+        try:
+            self.client.update_weights(
+                asdict(SparseDiskWeightTransferUpdateInfo(patch_path=str(path)))
+            )
+        finally:
+            path.unlink(missing_ok=True)

  | Model | TP | Patch per step | send_weights | reload_weights | Weights differing |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Qwen3-4B (8 GB) | 2 | 468-531 MB | 0.85-1.00 s | 1.74-2.23 s | 0 of 872 |

Weights on every rank matched both reload_weights and a cold start. Greedy outputs matched 8/8. The time gap got smaller as the patch grew

 A memory note! - Llama ran out of VRAM during the update at --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85. The sparse loader
  makes a full-size tensor per weight and the embedding alone is ~1 GB. It worked at 0.6
